text.p: These are the leading stories in the Malawi press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Spokesman for the ruling United Democratic Front (UDF), Cassim Chilumpha, has dismissed as false claims that his party bought off People's Democratic Party (PDP) defector Steven Mambuza who gave up his candidacy in Machinga North parliamentary by-elecions to join the UDF.
- Vendors in Lilongwe city market have vowed to defy orders by city officials to vacate their stalls.

- The World Bank in Malawi said the government's decision to increase public servant salaries on April 1 will have a negative effect on the country's economy unless government cuts its budget allocation to other services or increases taxes.
- Police expelled 49 recruits for allegedly falling short of the required height although they had undergone medical examinations in 1995 and trained for 12 days this year.
- President Bakili Muluzi's official vehicle was damaged at the weekend while travelling in a convoy when it hit a stray cow in Lilongwe, police said.
- A hyena bit off the hand of a man and attacked several other people in Ntcheu in central Malawi. The animal was later killed.
- More than 35 families have been left homeless after floods at the weekend in the Lunzu township north of Blantyre.
- The opposition Malawi Congress Party (MCP) and Alliance for Democracy (AFORD) met in secret in Rumphi after a group of clergy failed in mediation with the ruling United Democratic Front (UDF).
- Malawi fiscal police are probing the activities of former politician and human rights activist Aaron Longwe for alleged involvement in fraud and theft.
